title: Rigveda 1.76: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.76: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.76 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 52r-52v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.76.1-4 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 5, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 52r
translation.original_text:
1kā ta̱ upe̍ti̱r mana̍so̱ varā̍ya̱ bhuva̍d agne̱ śaṁta̍mā̱ kā ma̍nī̱ṣā | ko vā̍ ya̱jñaiḥ pari̱ dakṣa̍ṁ ta āpa̱ kena̍ vā te̱ mana̍sā dāśema ||
2ehy a̍gna i̱ha hotā̱ ni ṣī̱dāda̍bdha̱ḥ su pu̍rae̱tā bha̍vā naḥ | ava̍tāṁ tvā̱ roda̍sī viśvami̱nve yajā̍ ma̱he sau̍mana̱sāya̍ de̱vān ||
3pra su viśvā̍n ra̱kṣaso̱ dhakṣy a̍gne̱ bhavā̍ ya̱jñānā̍m abhiśasti̱pāvā̍ | athā va̍ha̱ soma̍pati̱ṁ hari̍bhyām āti̱thyam a̍smai cakṛmā su̱dāvne̍ ||
4pra̱jāva̍tā̱ vaca̍sā̱ vahni̍r ā̱sā ca̍ hu̱ve ni ca̍ satsī̱ha de̱vaiḥ | veṣi̍ ho̱tram u̱ta po̱traṁ ya̍jatra bo̱dhi pra̍yantar janita̱r vasū̍nām ||
translation.text:
1How may the mind draw nigh to please thee, Agni? What hymn of praise shall bring us greatest blessing? Or who hath gained thy power by sacrifices? or with what mind shall we bring thee oblations?
2Come hither, Agni; sit thee down as Hotar; be thou who never wast deceived our leader. May Heaven and Earth, the all-pervading, love thee: worship the Gods to win for us their favour.
3Burn thou up all the Riksasas, O Agni; ward thou off curses from our sacrifices. Bring hither with his Bays the Lord of Soma: here is glad welcome for the Bounteous Giver.
4Thou Priest with lip and voice that bring us children hast been invoked. Here with the Gods be seated. Thine is the task of Cleanser and Presenter: waken us, Wealth-bestower and Producer.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 52r (OPenn image 53, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.75.2 ‹-sānasi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 52v, begins in RV 1.76.5 ‹-eva hotariti satya-tara tvam›. Verses 1.76.1-4 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 1.76.5 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 5, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 52v
translation.original_text: <sup>5</sup>yathā̱ vipra̍sya̱ manu̍ṣo ha̱virbhi̍r de̱vām̐ aya̍jaḥ ka̱vibhi̍ḥ ka̱viḥ san | e̱vā ho̍taḥ satyatara̱ tvam a̱dyāgne̍ ma̱ndrayā̍ ju̱hvā̍ yajasva ||
translation.text: <sup>5</sup>As with oblations of the priestly Manus thou worshippedst the Gods, a Sage with sages, So now, O truthfullest Invoker Agni, worship this day with joy-bestowing ladle.
